claims.text: In as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys, magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are primarily governed by short-range chemical ordering and associated lattice strain.
Rapid deposition leaves incomplete atomic ordering that generates the relevant chemical disorder and lattice strain.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy is predominantly a disordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy contains intrinsic local chemical inhomogeneities and strain fields.
Annealing at 200–300°C followed by rapid quenching can promote short-range ordering without causing a complete phase transformation.
Annealing modifies or relieves lattice strain at grain or sub-grain boundaries.
Annealing enhances local atomic ordering and reduces chemical disorder.
Changes in chemical order and internal strain alter the energetic balance of the magnetostructural transition.
Changes in chemical order and internal strain alter barriers for magnetic-domain rearrangement.
The annealed material will have a less abrupt magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited material.
The annealed material will have a reduced hysteresis width under low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The annealed material will retain a substantial but more moderate and reversible magnetocaloric entropy change.
Temperature-dependent magnetic behavior will correlate with measurable changes in local chemical order.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi baseline exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with high hysteretic losses under low-field cooling cycles.
Annealing at excessive temperature may cause a complete phase transformation and invalidate the predicted behavior.
The proposed behavior may not transfer to alloy systems with different chemical complexity.
